title: Words from Italy
kidRule: Many food and music words came from Italian. They often have a double letter in the middle, and they usually end with a vowel you can hear, like A, I, or O!
hint: This word came from Italy! Say it slowly, the Italian way, and listen to every beat, especially the very end.
reminder: Italian words often have a double letter in the middle and usually end with a vowel like A, I, or O. Check both spots!

check.question: Why is CONFETTI spelled with two Ts and an I at the end?
check.correctAnswer: It came from Italian, where words often have double letters and usually end in a vowel!
distractors: Because every party word has a double letter
Because one T is never allowed in the middle of a word

words.def: A mountain with an opening where hot melted rock can burst out.
words.sent: Smoke puffed out of the top of the volcano.
words.story: This word came from Italian. It is named after Vulcan, the Roman god of fire, and so is the island of Vulcano in Italy!
words.card: *Can* a *volcano* burp? Only when it drinks too much lava soda!

words.def: Tiny bits of colored paper that people throw at parties and parades.
words.sent: We tossed confetti into the air at the party.
words.story: In Italy, confetti first meant small sweets that people tossed at festivals. Italians still use the word for sugar-coated almonds!
words.card: Pop! The *confetti* landed *on* the sleepy cat's nose!

words.def: A room where an artist, dancer, or musician works.
words.sent: The painter keeps her brushes in a sunny studio.
words.story: This word came into English from Italian, and long before that from a Latin word about eager learning!
words.card: A *stu*bborn elephant painted polka dots all over the art *studio*!

words.def: A dancer who performs on a stage, often up on the tips of her toes.
words.sent: The ballerina twirled across the stage.
words.story: This word is Italian. A busy ballerina can wear out a pair of toe shoes in a single show!
words.card: The *ballerina* balanced on a beach *ball* and spun like a top!

words.def: Long, thin noodles that look like strings.
words.sent: I twirled the spaghetti around my fork.
words.card: The noodles went to a *spa* and came out as relaxed *spaghetti*!

words.def: A green vegetable that looks like a bunch of tiny trees.
words.sent: I dipped my broccoli in cheese sauce.
words.story: Broccoli is an Italian word that means 'little sprouts'. The bumpy green tops are really bunches of flower buds!
words.card: The *col*d little tree in my lunchbox was really *broccoli*!

words.def: A folding cover on a stick that you hold over your head to stay dry in the rain.
words.sent: I opened my yellow umbrella when the rain began.
words.story: This word comes from an Italian word meaning 'little shade', because the first ones kept off the sun, not the rain!
words.card: The snail rang a b*ell* under its tiny *umbrella*!

words.def: Small noodles shaped like short, bent tubes.
words.sent: We stirred melted cheese into the macaroni.
words.story: This word comes from the Italian word 'maccheroni'. The little bent tubes are often called elbows!
words.card: A race *car* made of *macaroni* zoomed across my plate!

words.def: A soft, creamy frozen treat that is a lot like ice cream.
words.sent: We ate strawberry gelato in the sunny square.
words.story: In Italian, this word simply means 'frozen'!
words.card: The penguin put *gel* in its feathers before going out for *gelato*!

words.def: A long green vegetable that looks a bit like a cucumber.
words.sent: Grandpa grew a giant zucchini in his garden.
words.story: In Italian, this word means 'little squashes'!
words.card: The *zucchini* wore a tiny scarf under its *chin*!
